Below is a “tool‑kit” style cheat sheet covering the main ways you can **search, compare, book, and manage airline tickets**—from consumer‑facing portals all the way down to full‑blown B2B APIs that plug into your own app or website. | # | Tool / Service | What it does | Typical Use Case | Key Features & Notes | |---|-----------------|--------------|------------------|----------------------| | **A** | **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs**
*(Flight Offers Search, Ticketing, Availability, Pricing)* | Full end‑to‑end flight booking workflow. | Build a custom travel site, mobile app, or chatbot that lets users browse fares, select seats, pay, and receive e‑tickets. | • RESTful JSON
• Real‑time inventory + dynamic pricing
• Seat selection, baggage rules, ancillary sales
• Supports multiple currencies & languages
• Free tier available (limited calls); paid plans start at $99/mo | | **B** | **Sabre APIs** *(Global Distribution System – GDS)* | Classic distribution platform used by airlines, OTAs, corporate travel desks. | Enterprise‑grade solution where you need deep inventory coverage across legacy carriers. | • Extensive carrier network (~200+)
• Complex fare construction logic
• Requires a Sabre partner agreement
• Pay‑per‑request billing | | **C** | **Travelport Universal API** | Another leading GDS offering similar breadth to Sabre but with its own set of partners. | Corporate travel management, high‑volume ticketing. | • Unified interface for airlines, hotels, car rentals
• Advanced reporting & analytics
• Partner program required | | **D** | **Skyscanner RapidAPI** | Aggregated flight price index plus instant booking through partner integrations. | Quick prototype or low‑cost flight search widget. | • No direct ticket issuance (you redirect to partner’s checkout).
• Rate limits apply.
• Good for price comparison dashboards. | | **E** | **Kiwi.com API** | AI‑driven multi‑segment itineraries (“virtual interlining”). | Offer unique routes combining different airlines that don’t normally cooperate. | • Dynamic routing algorithm
• Instant booking & payment gateway built‑in
• Transparent cancellation policies | | **F** | **Expedia Affiliate Network (EAN)** | Bookings for flights, hotels, cars, packages. | Monetize traffic via affiliate commissions while providing complete travel bundles. | • Commission‑based revenue model
• Access to global inventory
• Requires EAN partnership | | **G** | **CheapOair API** | Focused on discounted airfare deals. | Target budget travelers looking for flash sales. | • Deals & coupons integrated
• Limited seat availability info compared to GDS | | **H** | **Google Flights (Unofficial)** | Web scraper/API wrappers around Google Flights’ UI. | When you only have a few queries per day and don't mind scraping. | • Not officially supported → risk of blocking
• Useful for research or small projects | | **I** | **OAG API** | Historical flight performance, schedule changes, delay statistics. | Airlines, airports, analysts needing operational insights rather than bookings. | • Big data focus
• Subscription‑only | | **J** | **Kayak, Momondo, Skyscanner, Expedia, Orbitz, Travelocity, Hotwire, Priceline, TripAdvisor** | Consumer‑facing aggregators & marketplaces. | End‑users searching for best prices, comparing options, making purchases directly on their sites. | • Each has its own UX/UI and commission structures | --- ### How to Pick the Right One | Decision Factor | Recommended Choice(s) | |-----------------|-----------------------| | **Need real‑time inventory & ticket issuing** | *Amadeus*, *Sabre*, *Travelport* | | **Want simple price lookup only** | *Skyscanner RapidAPI*, *Kiwi.com* (for virtual interlines) | | **Looking for a white‑label booking widget** | *Expedia Affiliate Network*, *CheapoAir* | | **Targeting budget travellers** | *CheapOair*, *Hotwire* | | **Building a marketplace** | Combine several APIs (e.g., Amadeus + Skyscanner) | | **Low volume, prototyping** | *RapidAPI* endpoints or even scraped data | --- #### Quick Code Snippet (Python) ```python import requests def amadeus_flight_search(origin='NYC', destination='LON', departure_date='2026-07-01'): url = ("https://test.api.amadeus.com/v2/shopping/flight-offers?" f"originLocationCode={origin}&destinationLocationCode={destination}" f"&departureDate={departure_date}") headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"} r = requests.get(url, headers=headers) return r.json() print(amadeus_flight_search()) ``` Replace `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with a token obtained after registering on the [Amadeus Developer Portal](https://developers.amadeus.com). --- ### Final Thoughts - **For developers building a brand‑new booking experience**, Amadeus offers the richest feature set with modern SDKs (JavaScript, Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby, Python). - **If you’re already working inside a larger enterprise system** that relies heavily on legacy carriers, consider partnering with Sabre or Travelport—they give you deeper control over complex fare rules. - **When cost matters more than depth**, cheap aggregation APIs (Skyscanner, Kiwi) let you surface competitive rates quickly without handling payments yourself. Feel free to tell me what kind of project you’re planning (consumer portal vs. corporate desk vs. data science study) and I’ll help narrow down the exact endpoint or combination of services!
